newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: DUBOIS HEADS TO ADELAIDE
One of the solo yachtsmen rescued from the Southern Ocean will be in Adelaide this afternoon for a reception at the RAAF base at Edinburgh.
Frenchman Thierry Dubois will meet the flight crews of the Adelaide-based Orions, used in the missions to rescue him and fellow yachstmen Raphael Dinelli and Tony Bullimore.
The Governor, Sir Eric Neale, Premier John Olsen and the Defence Minister, Ian MacLachlan, will attend the reception.
HAWKE MENTIONED AS POSSIBLE MEDIATOR IN JOCKEYS DISPUTE
A national, independent mediator could be called in to help resolve the pay dispute between jockeys and racing clubs.
The Australian Workers Union has confirmed that former Prime Minister Bob Hawke's name has been floated as a possible contender.
John Longhurst, an organiser from the AWU, says it may be necessary to bring in someone like Mr Hawke if current negotiations don't resolve the dispute.
NEW COPY IN AD TO MAKE VICTORIA LOOK BETTER
The Australian Tourist Commission has agreed to make immediate copy changes to an overseas promotion, that gives positive descriptions of Sydney beaches, but puts Victoria in a poor light.
Victorian Liberal MLC, David Davis, says all states should be equally promoted.
Mr Davis says the ATC's kit describes Victorian waters as colder than northern states and while this may be true, it's not the sort of overseas promotion Victoria's wants to push.
The promotion, on the other hand, offers descriptions for Sydney such as "Bondi Beach is compulsory".
Mr Davis says Tourism Victoria will rewrite the copy to highlight Victoria's attractions.
BEATTIE SAYS NO TO KING CHARLES OF QUEENSLAND
Queenslanders don't want Prince Charles to be King of Queensland, according to State Opposition Leader Peter Beattie.
Amendments to the State's Constitution under the former Bjelke-Petersen Government describe Elizabeth the Second as the Queen of Queensland.
Mr Beattie says while there is a lot of support for the Queen, there's not the same backing for her son.
He says in his view, Prince Charles has behaved in a similar way to a soap opera star.
Mr Beattie's called for a wide-ranging pubic debate leading up to 2000, as to whether Queenslanders want Prince Charles to be King Charles of Queensland.
WASTE HANDLING AT SYDNEY AIRPORT
The Quarantine Service says it has already taken steps to improve procedures for handling waste from Sydney's international airport.

New South Wales MP, Paul Gibson, has raised fears that mishandling of airport waste poses a significant risk to agricultural industries, and is calling on the Federal Government to review quarantine practices.

The Acting National Manager of the Quarantine Service, Denis Ayliffe, says he's aware of waste being spilt during transportation to the Castlereagh dump in western Sydney, and of delays in waste being treated.
But he says the problems were fixed several weeks ago.
RESCUE EXPECTED TO BOOST NAVY RECRUITS
The Royal Australian Navy is expecting the dramatic and high profile rescue of the two solo yachtsmen from the Southern Ocean to boost recruiting.
The navy's director of recruiting, Commander Bob Nelson, says it's too early for eager recruits to be knocking on their door, but the publicity should lead to more interest in the Navy.
Commander Nelson says the publicity given to HMAS Adelaide's rescue has shed a more positive light on life in the Navy.
LEHMANN AND REIFFEL JOIN AUSSIE TEAM
South Australia's Darren Lehmann and Victorian Paul Reiffel are in the Australian side for Thursday's limited over cricket international against Pakistan in Melbourne.
Reiffel replaces West Australian Tom Moody who's been dropped, while Lehman replaces the injured Mark Waugh.
The rest of the squad is Taylor captain, Healey vice captain, Bevan, Bichel, Blewett, Law, McGrath, Stuart, Warne and Steve Waugh.
WIND TUNNEL TO SAVE LIVES, SAYS CSIRO
The CSIRO says a wind tunnel it's unveiled can help fire brigades predict how embers will travel ahead of a bushfire and create spot fires.
The vertical wind tunnel will be used to provide world-leading research into the spot-fires which start from bushfires.
The CSIRO says spot fires pose a great danger for fire-fighters because little is known about their behaviour.
Researcher Phil Cheney says better advice will be given to firefighters, increasing safety.
